newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO CELEBRATE AFTER 2-0 AWAY WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO CELEBRATE AFTER 2-0 AWAY WIN.

text.p: Monaco all but won the French first division championship when they beat Strasbourg 2-0 away on Tuesday to take an unsurpassable 12-point lead with three games remaining.

The Monaco players celebrated in the dressing room after goals from strikers Anderson and Victor Ikpeba had given them a victory that will take the title to the principality for the sixth time barring a miracle by Paris St Germain.
Monaco president Jean-Louis Campora: "It's too soon to drink champagne, but it does look good."
If the European Cup Winners' Cup finalists, long resigned to the fight for second place, drop points at Lille on Wednesday they will hand the title to Monaco.
To retain any chance, the Parisian side must win all their remaining matches, while Monaco must lose all theirs and squander a goal difference that is 11 better than PSG's.

Anderson broke the deadlock in the 64th minute when Belgian defender Philippe Leonard turned a long free kick from Ali Benarbia back into the middle from the left and the Brazilian had only to tap the ball in.
Monaco survived a scare when Strasbourg's top scorer David Zitelli was just wide with a diving header a minute later.
Ikpeba secured the points for Monaco in the 77th minute when he cracked a shot past Klein's despairing dive and into the roof of the net from the left.

Monaco, wary of a side that beat them 2-1 on the same ground in their League Cup semifinal in February, started slowly and in the opening minutes, goalkeeper Fabien Barthez had to save with his foot from forward Gerald Baticle.
But, after an even first half with few other chances, Monaco presaged their goal with three good openings in the first 15 minutes after the interval.

Midfielder Sylvain Legwinski headed just over from a corner, Brazilian Anderson also put the ball above the bar when he lobbed David Klein and the goalkeeper also blocked a shot by Ikpeba with his leg.
The Monaco defence kept a tight rein on striker Pascal Nouma, who scored all Strasbourg's goals in their 4-1 win at Montpellier on Saturday.
At the bottom end of the table, Caen's relegation worries increased with a 1-0 defeat at home by Montpellier. Striker Laurent Robert scored in the 53rd minute.
The Normandy side remain one from bottom and four points behind Le Havre, the lowest placed team outside the four relegation places.
